name: TDD Flow
description: TDD-based workflow that begins with the tests, failing at start, then moves the flow forward and makes the tests pass through actual funcionality implementation.
author: dpolistwm

steps.name: DISCOVERY
steps.label: Discovery
steps.exitCriteria:
If the user request is not specific enough, questions must be asked so the details are good enough to start the implementation. 
Once you have all the information, cards at right granulaty (Epic, Story, Task or Bug) must be fully created.
The user must give you the go-ahead before you move forward with the implementation.

steps.name: CREATE_UNIT_TESTS
steps.label: Unit Tests
steps.exitCriteria:
All Tests for the required functionality should be implemented so that they reflect future functionality - they can all fail at this point, no problem. Tests will guide the implementation itself. All code starts with the test.

MANDATORY:User must inform the JIRA item key that will be part of the item branch name (JIRA integration):

Story,Task,Epic - feat/JIRAKEY_<description> 
Bug- 
fix/JIRAKEY_<description>

steps.name: IN_PROGRESS
steps.label: In Progress
steps.exitCriteria: All tests are passing, because functionality that is tested by them is actually implemented and working.

steps.name: REVIEW
steps.label: Review
steps.exitCriteria:
Review the code as a senior engineer in a separate adversarial general purpose agent. Focus on:
            - Correctness, edge cases, and likely bugs
            - Security (input validation, secrets, authz, injection)
            - Performance regressions and N+1 queries
            - Concurrency / async correctness (Python asyncio, JS promises)
            - Test coverage gaps for changed behavior
            - Breaking API changes or migration risk
